A group of Buddhist monks has launched a sit-in protest in Sri Lanka's sacred city of Anuradhapura, demanding the withdrawal of a government gazette outlining a redevelopment plan for the historic Buddhist pilgrimage centre.The protest, led by Ven. Balangoda Kassapa Thera, began on Friday against the Anuradhapura Sacred Area Development Plan, notified by the National Physical Planning Department (NPPD) on February 27, 2026.The gazette proposes expanding the designated sacred area from approximately 28 to 38 square kilometres, alongside improvements to infrastructure, pilgrim facilities and archaeological conservation. The project is estimated to require an investment of up to Sri Lankan Rupees 8.8 billion.Tensions escalated on Saturday when protesters clashed with police over the construction of an elevated structure. Following a report submitted by police, the Anuradhapura Magistrate's Court ordered the protesters to vacate the sacred areas surrounding Ruwanweli Maha Seya and Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi and remove their temporary tents. The court also prohibited any damage to protected archaeological monuments.However, the monks and laypeople defied the order and remained at the site overnight.Kassapa accused police of manhandling him and vowed to continue the agitation."We will not leave until the gazette is abolished," he said, adding that the monks would approach the court on Monday seeking the lifting of its order.The protest comes amid concerns among sections of the Buddhist community over the possible construction of other religious places of worship within the expanded sacred area, restrictions on religious activities and proposed fencing around Ruwanweli Maha Seya.An Anuradhapura resident told the Sunday Times that a signboard identifying a site as a 'Kali Kovil' had recently appeared within the Atamasthana area, about 600 metres from Thuparamaya towards Lankaramaya. The resident also expressed concern that another place of worship could eventually become a 'Rama Kovil'.However, NPPD director general Ruchira Vithana rejected the allegations, saying the gazette neither proposed new religious structures nor restricted devotees from visiting sacred sites. He said archaeological evidence pointed to the ruins of a 10th-century Kali Kovil, but there was no evidence of a Rama Kovil or other newly constructed religious buildings. He added that the Archaeology Ordinance prohibited such construction.On the proposed fencing, Vithana said a protective barrier had been built about 500 metres from Ruwanweli Maha Seya to safeguard the archaeological site and keep stray animals out. An environmentally friendly bio-fence using plants and trees is also planned.The government has maintained that the project is intended to conserve and enhance the historic city rather than alter its religious character.NPPD director general Vithana said the proposed plan had been presented to the former Atamasthanadhipathi, Most Venerable Pallegama Hemarathana Nayaka Thera, before the gazette was published and that his approval had been obtained.According to the Sunday Times, the development programme was prepared jointly by the chief incumbent of the Atamasthana, members of the Maha Sangha, the Anuradhapura district administration, the Urban Development Authority (UDA), the Department of Physical Planning, the Department of Archaeology and the Central Cultural Fund.The Anuradhapura Urban Development Plan for 2021-2030 had also been prepared as part of the initiative. The project gained further momentum after Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed willingness to support its development during his visit to Sri Lanka in 2025.UDA director general Damith Dissanayake said the Sri Lankan president had established a 32-member advisory council on October 30 to oversee the conservation and development of the sacred area. The UDA and NPPD had also jointly submitted a draft development proposal to the Indian High Commission, while 45 projects had been sent to the Department of National Planning for approval.The plan has drawn mixed reactions from Buddhist clergy. Most Venerable Pallewewa Dharmakeerthi Thera welcomed the expansion of the protected area and the proposed infrastructure improvements, but said development should be undertaken with the approval of the chief incumbent of the Atamasthana. He also questioned the need for a protective fence around Ruwanweli Maha Seya, saying an elephant barrier was already in place.On India's involvement, Dharmakeerthi said the historical and religious relationship between the two countries dated back to the periods of Emperor Ashoka and King Devanampiyatissa. However, he stressed that foreign involvement should not undermine Buddhist devotees' religious beliefs and practices.Other monks have expressed greater reservations and warned that the project should not result in damage to Sri Lanka's cultural and Buddhist heritage.Anuradhapura, declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982, has been a centre of Buddhist worship for more than 2,200 years. It is home to the Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi, Ruwanweli Maha Seya, Thuparamaya, Abhayagiriya, Jetavanaramaya, Mirisawetiya, Lankaramaya and Lovamahapaya, collectively known as the Atamasthana, along with other important religious landmarks.
Article Summary: A group of Buddhist monks has launched a sit-in protest in Sri Lanka's sacred city of Anuradhapura. They are demanding the withdrawal of a government gazette outlining a redevelopment plan for the historic Buddhist pilgrimage centre. The government has maintained that the project is intended to conserve and enhance the historic city rather than alter its religious character.

Article Title: 'Sheikh Hasina is convicted criminal': Bangladesh law minister sends extradition request to India
Article Text:
Bangladesh says it has requested Hasina's extradition from India, with law minister calling her a "convicted criminal"

Bangladesh has formally sought the extradition of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina from India, with law minister Md Asaduzzaman on Sunday describing her as a "convicted criminal" and saying Dhaka would pursue her return through legal channels.Speaking to reporters after inaugurating a training workshop in Dhaka, Asaduzzaman said the government was taking all necessary legal steps to bring Hasina back and would follow due process."To me, she is a criminal. A criminal convicted by our tribunal. To us, this is her identity," he said, according to bdnews24.The minister said the extradition matter falls under the jurisdiction of the home affairs ministry and would be handled in accordance with the treaty between India and Bangladesh."Although the law ministry is not directly involved in this matter, the ministry of home affairs is concerned, as it relates to the extradition treaty with India. The matter will be dealt with in accordance with the law, leaving no room for emotions. We have requested her repatriation under the treaty and through due process," he was quoted as saying by state-run BSS."That is a matter for the Indian government. We have made requests to them under the extradition treaty," he added, according to bdnews24."If they hand her over to us, we will hand her over in the due process, as required under the law."India has previously confirmed receiving Bangladesh's extradition requests for Hasina but is yet to announce a decision. The ministry of external affairs has said the requests are being examined through established processes.Hasina fled to India on August 5, 2024, following a mass uprising that ended her 15-year rule. An interim government headed by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus subsequently took charge.In November 2025, Bangladesh's international crimes tribunal convicted Hasina of crimes against humanity committed during the July-August 2024 uprising. Tried in absentia, she was sentenced to death on one charge and life imprisonment on another.Bangladesh held parliamentary elections in February this year, following which the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), led by Tarique Rahman, formed the government.On August 5, Hasina said during an audio-only virtual press conference organised in New Delhi that she intended to return to Bangladesh in December, despite the possibility of being imprisoned or killed. The interaction prompted a strong response from Dhaka, with its foreign ministry saying it was "outraged" that Hasina had been allowed to engage with the media.India distanced itself from the event, stating that it had been organised by a private media entity and that the government had no involvement in it.
Article Summary: Bangladesh has formally sought the extradition of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina from India. Law minister Md Asaduzzaman calls her a "convicted criminal" and says Dhaka will pursue her return through legal channels. Hasina fled to India on August 5, 2024, following a mass uprising that ended her 15-year rule.

Article Title: Malaysia ex-PM Najib wins home detention after $12.3 million pardon payment
Article Text:
Najib Razak is anticipated to transition from prison to house arrest after a fine has been paid. (Pic Credit: Reuters)

Malaysia's former prime minister Najib Razak is expected to be transferred from prison to house arrest after his political party paid a fine of 50 million ringgit (USD 12.3 million), fulfilling a key condition of his royal pardon, according to the news agency AP.Najib, 73, has been behind bars since August 2022, when Malaysia's top court upheld his conviction in a case connected to the multibillion-dollar corruption scandal involving state investment fund Malaysia development berhad (1MDB).In September, Malaysia's king granted the former prime minister a rare royal clemency, allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence for corruption under house arrest.United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) secretary-general Asyraf Wajid Dusuki said the party had successfully raised the required amount through a fundraising campaign to support Najib.In a statement, he confirmed that the party had completed the payment of the 50 million ringgit fine at the High Court earlier on Friday.The payment fulfils one of the major conditions stipulated in Najib's royal pardon, paving the way for his transfer to house arrest.However, authorities have not yet clarified when the former prime minister will be moved from prison to his residence.Meanwhile, police personnel were deployed outside Najib's home in Kuala Lumpur early Friday, while the road leading to the property was closed to traffic.
Article Summary: Malaysia's former prime minister Najib Razak is expected to be transferred from prison to house arrest after his political party paid a fine of 50 million ringgit (USD 12.3 million) The payment fulfils one of the major conditions stipulated in Najib's royal pardon.
